observations: Photo 0 shows a large rectangular solar panel with a dark glass surface and grid lines; no visible brand/model label.
Photo 1 shows the same style solar panel from a different angle; still no readable rating sticker (Wattage, Voc, Isc, brand/model).
Both photos show the panel outdoors/near a building; there are reflections and a visible watermark text on the image, but no clear product identification.

claims.claim: High Quality Solar Panels, Inverters, Lithium & Tubular Batteries, Charge...
claims.evidence: Seller text only; photos show only a solar panel and no inverter/battery/charge controller.

risks.risk: Panel wattage/efficiency class is unknown (price depends heavily on Wp rating like 100W/150W/200W+).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the panel’s label/sticker showing brand, model, and electrical ratings (Wp, Voc, Isc, Vmp, Imp).
risks.if_unproven: Price as the lowest common/unknown-spec solar panel (worst case: lower wattage and standard performance).

risks.risk: Condition risk: possible shipping damage, micro-cracks, or water ingress not visible in these reflections.
risks.proof: Photos of the panel edges/frame and backsheet, plus a close-up of the glass for cracks; also a video showing it under light (or an IV test report).
risks.if_unproven: Price as used/possibly damaged (worst case: treat as not guaranteed to be defect-free).

risks.risk: Compatibility risk: connector type and cable length may not match the buyer’s system (MC4 vs other, length, polarity).
risks.proof: Photo of the junction box and connectors (close-up), including connector type and cable length measurement.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming basic compatibility but without confirming connector/cable details (worst case: buyer may need adapters).

risks.risk: Authenticity/brand risk: the panel could be generic or mismatched to the seller’s “high quality” claim.
risks.proof: Label photo with brand/model and serial number (if present) and a matching photo of the same label on the physical unit.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic/unknown brand (worst case: no premium brand value).

proof_requests: Send a close-up photo of the panel rating label/sticker (brand, model, Wp, Voc, Isc, Vmp, Imp).
Send a clear photo of the junction box + connector type (MC4 or other) and cable length.
Send close-ups of the glass surface and frame edges for cracks/chips, plus a backsheet photo.
If possible, provide an IV test report or a simple performance test reading (measured Vmp/Imp under sun).
response.reason: The photos confirm it’s a solar panel, but the key pricing driver (brand/model and wattage rating) is not readable, and condition/connector details can’t be verified from these images. Without the label, any price would be guesswork.
